title: Microflow run tracker - Eli
content:
Quick personal tracker for small-batch microflows (handy when I need to compare cost/latency tradeoffs quickly)

Header: one-page snapshot, keep it terse, update after each run.

Columns (CSV-style for easy copy/paste): run_id, date, model, variant, quant, batch_sz, seq_len, route (hosted/dedicated), p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_out, cost_est_per_1k, notes, next_step

Sample rows:
r001, 2025-01-08, llama-3-8b, base, int8, 1, 128, hosted, 42, 96, 640, $0.95, baseline single-token latency looks fine, try kv-cache
r002, 2025-01-10, vicuna-13b, q4f16, q4f16, 4, 256, dedicated, 85, 190, 3,200, $0.70, batching improves throughput but tail spikes; check GPU mem fragmentation
r003, 2025-01-15, llm-small, cache-enabled, int8, 8, 64, hosted, 28, 60, 1,920, $0.35, prefix caching reduced p50 by ~30%, confirm accuracy on prompt set
r004, 2025-01-22, redwood-optim-7b, kv-off, int8, 1, 1024, private, 150, 340, 5,120, $1.80, long-context regressed; need kernel-tune

Quick notes-to-self:
- When seq_len > 512, kernel selection changes and p95 jumps; record kernel version in notes if possible.
- Always include tokens_out for rough cost math. I tend to forget.
- For dedicated runs, note node type (A100/RTX) in next step if anomalies.
- If p95/p50 ratio > 3, mark as "spiky" in notes and tag run for deeper profiling.

Mini checklist before entering run row:
- Confirm model path + commit hash (if dev model)
- Seed + eval prompts (small set of 10)
- Billing tier (hosted vs dedicated)
- Any config overrides (e.g., disable kv-cache)

Daily microflow goals (personal):
- 1 reproducible run with full notes (every 2 days)
- 3 quick compare runs when testing batching/quant changes
- flag 1 anomaly for SRE/profiler if spikes observed

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add a tiny snippet to automatically compute cost_est_per_1k from token counts and price table. (GH#4871)
- Create a consistent short-code for kernel versions (k1, k2) to keep rows compact.
- Share this layout with Maya and Raf for quick alignment — ask Maya to paste node type in notes.

Random scribbles:
- If latency is stable but quality drops after quant -> run evalset A (10 prompts) and attach small delta score in notes.
- Remember: caching good for steady throughput but can mask cold-start issues.

End of sheet. Keep it light, keep it usable.
